sourceCaveatNotes.title: Reader note: native whole tasks and printed footer labels
sourceCaveatNotes.statement: The original question booklet contains Q1, Compressible fluids (12 requests); Q2, Sources, atoms, and spectra (6 requests); and Theoretical Problem No. 3, “Squeezing” electrical charge carriers using magnetic fields (11 requests). These are three whole problems with 29 connected requests. Q1 and Q2 pages print “Theoretical Problem No. 3” in their recurring footer. The body titles and connected parts establish the problem grouping; the printed footer labels remain in the original PDF.

sourceCaveatNotes.title: Reader note: retained key authority and original mathematical expressions
sourceCaveatNotes.statement: The retained solutions_2016.pdf carries Romanian Master of Physics 2016 branding, matching Q1 and Q2 worked keys, and a detailed Q3 grading scheme credited to the named problem authors. It is a key retained by the archive; an organizer publication URL has not been independently verified. The solutions are attributed to the archive. Q1 key equations are small embedded raster images; their printed mathematical content is retained.

sourceCaveatNotes.title: Reader note: literal flow and shock-key calculations
sourceCaveatNotes.statement: The B3.1 repeated key stem omits the original question’s condition $v<c$; the condition remains in the question. B3.2 prints $p_s=p+\rho v^2$, $v=276\ \mathrm{m/s}$ and $M=0.802$. Those printed expressions and values are retained. The shock derivation denotes the undisturbed gas by $p,\rho$, while the question uses $p_s,\rho_s$; each source notation remains in its original context.

sourceCaveatNotes.title: Reader note: literal shock equation and numerical discrepancy
sourceCaveatNotes.statement: C2.2 prints its final shock-speed factor as $c\sqrt{(x_1y_1-1)/(\gamma x_1-1)}$. C2.3 then prints $341\times0.775=264\ \mathrm{m/s}$ after C2.2 reports Mach 3.58. Those algebraic and numerical forms do not consistently follow the preceding relations. C2.1 prints its final ratio $T_1/T$ without a denominator subscript. These literal source expressions are preserved.

sourceCaveatNotes.title: Reader note: answer-sheet title correspondence
sourceCaveatNotes.statement: Question page 9 labels the Sources, atoms, and spectra answer sheet Q3, while the matching question and key label it Q2. The six A/B/C requests, marks and content establish its correspondence to Q2. Both printed labels remain in the transcription and the original answer-sheet crop.

sourceCaveatNotes.title: Reader note: literal absorption-ratio ordering
sourceCaveatNotes.statement: The key’s displayed wavelength ratio uses its energy-difference numerator and denominator in the reciprocal order from the preceding inverse wavelength expression. It then prints $102.8/97.5=1.054$ and $0.054/n_1^2=1.054/n_2^2-1/(n_2+1)^2$. The printed ratio, search table and both estimates of $A$ are retained literally.

sourceCaveatNotes.title: Reader note: printed permeability unit and source language
sourceCaveatNotes.statement: The question prints the magnetic permeability of vacuum as $\mu_0=4\pi\times10^{-7}\ \mathrm{F\,m^{-1}}$. The unit is dimensionally anomalous for permeability; the printed F is retained. Task 3.iii contains the Romanian word “și” between $\mu$ and $k_B$, also retained.

sourceCaveatNotes.title: Reader note: complete Q3 rubric and literal source expressions
sourceCaveatNotes.statement: The matching Q3 key is the complete four-page “Detailed grading scheme”. Every intermediate formula, partial mark, both diagrams and the instruction to credit other correct approaches are retained. The rubric prints $\omega_0\cong5\times10^7\ \mathrm{rotations\,s^{-1}}$, a plus sign between the two component terms of $\vec F_{S.L.}$, its $+e$ potential-energy signs, and the displayed pressure-force differential signs. These expressions and the printed conclusions are preserved. No additional prose derivation is present in this source.

sourceCaveatNotes.title: Reader note: matching theory boundary and retained experimental tail
sourceCaveatNotes.statement: The question booklet contains fourteen pages covering the three theory problems and seven blank answer sheets. In the thirty-page key PDF, pages 1–10 correspond to Q1, pages 11–14 to Q2, and pages 15–18 to Q3. Pages 19–25 contain “Experimental Problem No. 1. Secrets of toys”, a filled answer and marking key for a hollow globe and an optical black box. Pages 26–30 contain the detailed grading scheme for “Experimental Problem Nr. 2. The study of Moiré pattern”. These experimental pages are retained in the original PDF, but are outside the matching theory scope. The exact retained event folder lists only problems_2016.pdf and solutions_2016.pdf; no matching experimental question booklet or further companion was obtainable there.
